summary: T6 wires WebViewBridge insight messages and EditorView routing cleanly: 5 Swift→JS commands with the array-wrap encoding helper, 5 JS→Swift dispatch cases, WebViewBridgeDelegate extended with 5 stubs, and a Coordinator.routeInsight that subscribes via Combine with `[weak self, weak session, weak webView]` and main-queue ordering for currentNodeId/streamingBuffer. Build succeeds, all naming/structure/payload encoding match spec; one cross-task snapshot UX bug (tab-switch-during-stream loses already-buffered text because session.snapshot().markdown is markdownBody not rawBuffer) and a couple of minor robustness suggestions are noted below.

suggestions.suggestion: Tab-switch-during-stream causes visible data loss in the JS view. routeInsight calls bridge.loadInsightView(snapshot:) — InsightSession.snapshot() returns `markdown: cur?.markdownBody ?? ""` (Models/InsightSession.swift:513). markdownBody is only populated in finalizeStream after the stream finishes. So when the user switches AWAY from a streaming insight tab and back, JS gets an empty markdown payload and lastForwardedLength is snapped to streamingBuffer.count, so the already-buffered N chars are never replayed and future deltas append onto an empty pane. This contradicts tech-spec Decision 11 §5 ("switching back re-renders from current streamingBuffer snapshot, no data loss") and the corresponding acceptance criterion at line 500/517 of tech-spec.md.
suggestions.benefit: Matches the spec's no-data-loss guarantee on tab switch during a live stream. Two viable fixes: (a) extend InsightViewSnapshot/snapshot() so streaming nodes serialise rawBuffer instead of markdownBody (cleanest, requires touching Task 4 contract), or (b) in routeInsight, after loadInsightView, immediately forward `appendInsightDelta(text: session.streamingBuffer)` when the session is mid-stream (lastForwardedLength is then already correct). Option (b) keeps T6 self-contained.

suggestions.suggestion: When switching from one .insight session to another .insight session, routeInsight resets `lastLoadedContent = ""` and `currentDocumentBaseURL = nil`. That's correct for invalidating file-side dedupe, but the comment says "so a subsequent switch back to a .file tab is forced to re-render from scratch (the WebView's content is now insight)". The comment is right; consider also calling `bridge.showInsightLoading(...)` (the new T6 command) between the old session's last render and the new snapshot, so the user sees feedback during the cross-session paint.
suggestions.benefit: More polished transition UX; the showInsightLoading command was added in this task but is currently unreferenced anywhere in the EditorView routing path.

suggestions.suggestion: `lastForwardedLength` and `newBuffer.count` use Character (extended grapheme cluster) counting via Swift's String semantics. This is consistent with `streamingBuffer.append(chunk)` in InsightSession (also Character-based), so deltas will not split a grapheme. Worth a one-line comment noting the invariant — it is non-obvious to a future reader and a tempting "optimization" might switch to .utf8.count to avoid O(n) scanning, which would silently corrupt multibyte/emoji boundaries.
suggestions.benefit: Documents the invariant so a future reader doesn't break it. No behavioural change.

suggestions.suggestion: loadInsightView and setInsightDeepDives create a fresh JSONEncoder each call. Cheap but allocation-y on hot paths (every navigation triggers loadInsightView). Consider hoisting `private static let jsonEncoder = JSONEncoder()` and reusing it. JSONEncoder is thread-safe for encoding once configured.
suggestions.benefit: Tiny perf win, removes a per-call allocation on the navigation path.

suggestions.suggestion: The 5 NSLog stubs for insight delegate methods are correctly intentional (Task 7 wires them). Consider adding `// MARK: - Task 7 wires these` and grouping them at the bottom of the extension so a code search for the TODO finds the seam. Currently the comment block is only above the first stub.
suggestions.benefit: Easier handoff to Task 7; the TODO seam is more discoverable.
